thread_text:
Maria G: FYI - after yesterday's kernel swap for Mistral-7B (attention v2 -> v3) we started seeing a subtle quality regression on the summarization eval set. Quick dump of findings below.

Jonas L: ugh. symptoms?

Maria G: small divergence in sentence ordering + occasional hallucinated dates. Mostly at context > 1024 tokens.

Alex H: sounds like a RoPE / position-decay issue to me. Did the kernel change touch rotary handling?

Maria G: yes — v3 switched to a fused attention kernel that uses scaled RoPE with dynamic scaling factor computed from seq_len distribution. We added a quick heuristic to avoid overflow for long sequences.

Kevin S: profiling numbers from canary:
```
before (v2): p99 latency 142ms, doc-level throughput 85 req/s, KV cache hit rate 0.72
after (v3): p99 latency 128ms, throughput 92 req/s, KV cache hit rate 0.66
```
Maria G: perf improved overall but KV hit drop and eval metric delta: rouge-L down 1.8 points on our long-doc eval set.

Jonas L: interesting. KV hit rate drop could explain content degradation if cache keys mismatch due to different key-projection numerics. Any quant changes?

Maria G: quant config unchanged. However the kernel uses a different fp16 accumulation path and slightly different head-splitting ordering which shifts rounding.

PerfBot: ALERT: eval/regression-check failed on run 2025-11-15T09:05Z (delta rouge-L -1.82, p-value 0.003).

Alex H: can we reproduce with deterministic seed and CPU fp32 path? If it's numeric drift we should see it.

Maria G: repro steps I ran:
```
# reproduce summary test
python evals/run_eval.py --model mistral-7b --backend runtime-v3 --seed 42 --dataset long-docs --max_len 2048
```
Result: mismatch vs v2 at ~token 1143 consistently.

Kevin S: that token boundary screams RoPE wrap/scale issue. When seq_len > 1024 our dynamic scale multiplies cos/sin by factor 0.87 to keep values stable. Maybe that interacts poorly with legacy positional embedding expectations.

Sara P: product impact? Are we seeing customer regressions or just internal eval?

Maria G: only detected internally so far but the eval set is representative of some customer workloads (long summaries). Suggest we either revert kernel or tweak RoPE scaling.

Jonas L: do we have an experiment to isolate kernel swap vs rope scaling vs head-ordering?

Maria G: plan I propose:
- run v3 but force legacy RoPE (scale=1.0)
- run v3 where we only change head-ordering back to v2 ordering
- run v3 with full fp32 accumulation enabled (slower)
Each run will produce perf + quality deltas and KV hit rate.

Alex H: I'll own the head-ordering test. Jonas can you force fp32 accumulation on the kernel?

Jonas L: yep, can toggle a compile flag. Will run night job and post results.

Kevin S: if head-ordering fixes KV hit we can ship a micro-fix. If not, fallback is to revert kernel to v2 for Mistral until we have a robust numeric path.

PerfBot: NOTE: rollback option created - PR #4123 (revert runtime-v3 for mistral-7b)

Maria G: I started different eval runs; summary of initial quick runs:
- v3 + legacy-rope (scale=1.0): rouge-L delta -0.12, KV hit 0.71, latency p99 130ms
- v3 + head-order=v2: rouge-L delta -0.45, KV hit 0.70
- v3 + fp32-accum: rouge-L delta -0.05, KV hit 0.72, latency p99 160ms

Sara P: looks like numeric accumulation is the main culprit but it increases latency a lot. Tradeoff: quality vs SLO.

Jonas L: fp32 fixes it best. legacy-rope mostly helps. Head-order not sufficient. This implies accumulation rounding is changing key/query vectors enough to affect cache keys.

Alex H: can we do a hybrid? Use fp16 accumulation for short sequences and fp32 for sequences > 1024 where we see drift? Kernel can auto-select based on seq_len.

Maria G: that's a good middle ground. Cost estimate: p99 for long requests will increase from 128ms -> ~150ms under fp32, but majority short requests unaffected. Need to test throughput impact on dedicated pools.

Kevin S: also consider improving KV cache key tolerance: use L2-normalized keys or coarse hashing to reduce sensitivity to tiny numeric drift. That may be cheaper than fp32 everywhere.

Jonas L: true. I'll prototype L2-normalized key hashing; should be a small patch. If we accept slightly higher false negatives, overall hit might improve.

PerfBot: ACTION: night runs queued: (1) v3+fp32-for-long, (2) v3+norm-keys, (3) v2 revert smoke. ETA 12h.

Maria G: thanks. If night runs show fp32-for-long fixes eval without huge throughput loss, we can patch rollout policy to enable kernel auto-fallback for long sequences and keep v3 for general traffic. Otherwise PR #4123 stands.

Kevin S: tagging @oncall for capacity planning if we switch to fp32 for a subset of traffic.

Sara P: keep product posted if rollback needed; we should prepare comms. :loudspeaker:

Alex H: one more note: quantized customers might experience different delta; make sure we run quantized evals too.

Maria G: good call — adding q4_0 and q2 evals to the matrix.

Jonas L: posting results when done.

Maria G: thanks all :heart:

PerfBot: job results: run 1 (v3+fp32-for-long) -> rouge-L delta -0.03, latency p99 (long) +18ms, KV hit restored. run 2 (v3+norm-keys) -> rouge-L delta -0.6, KV hit 0.69. run 3 (v2 revert) -> rouge-L delta baseline, latency p99 142ms.

Maria G: conclusion: fp32-for-long is acceptable tradeoff for now. I'll open a PR to add kernel auto-select fallback and enable it for Mistral in the rollout policy. Also will add a feature flag to revert if any customer complains.

Kevin S: ack. if PR merges, coordinate a small canary at 5% traffic then 20% ramp.

Sara P: prepping comms for support team.

Alex H: putting follow-up tasks in the runtime board.

Jonas L: closing loop when infra numbers from dedicated pools look good.

PerfBot: REMINDER: close regression incident if rollback not needed within 48h.
